title: Why the shelf you built feels special
summary: The IKEA effect: people value things more when they have put effort into making them — but only when the effort ends in success.
evidenceNote: Based on a small number of lab experiments, so the exact size of the effect is uncertain.

scenes.text: Why does the wobbly shelf you built yourself feel so special?
Researchers call it the IKEA effect: we value things more when we've put our own effort into making them.

items.title: Built IKEA boxes
items.detail: and would pay more for them than for pre-built ones

items.title: Folded origami
items.detail: and valued it close to an expert's work

scenes.text: Effort creates attachment — but only when it leads to something that works.
Two sides of the same effect.

left.label: Use it
left.text: Let people build part of something to value it

right.label: Watch out
right.text: You may overrate your own ideas and projects

scenes.text: Love what you build — but judge it with fresh eyes.

sources.title: The IKEA effect: When labor leads to love
